title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 57
text:
132. A person will not be permitted to perform the role of McKenzie Friend if unsuitable, eg if they
have an interest in any financial outcome of the case.

133. Guidance as to the circumstances in which permitting a McKenzie Friend in civil and family
proceedings will be appropriate, and related advice can be found in the “Practice Guidance
(McKenzie Friends: Civil and Family Courts)” issued by the Master of the Rolls and the
President of the Family Division on 12 July 2010.
Support Through Court and Citizens Advice

134. Litigants should also be aware of the services provided by Support Through Court
(previously known as the Personal Support Unit (PSU)). There are several Support Through
Court offices in various locations across the UK, but they are not universally available.
Volunteers provide free support in the civil and family courts and some tribunals, dealing with
issues such as contact with children, divorce, eviction and money claims. They explain how
courts work, discuss the concept of settlement, help with completing forms, help the LIP plan
